query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys have reported densities of 1.46–6 g/cm3 and commonly contain solid solutions together with intermetallic compounds. Earlier induction-melted Al–Mg-rich alloys established this structural complexity but did not resolve subsequent transformation pathways. Compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd alloys showed region-dependent compression and corrosion performance, while studies of AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys associated Mg content with phase stability and multiple functional properties. Most prior work emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, leaving corrosion, high-temperature oxidation, and evolution from metastable states comparatively underexplored. Within the design constraint of density below 6 g/cm3 and the tendency for constituent-property differences to promote stable intermetallic compounds, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain how a non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy evolves and why that evolution changes its corrosion and high-temperature oxidation behavior? Specify an unnamed controlled comparison, predictions relative to the initial baseline, boundary conditions, supporting prior observations, and an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Thermal aging of non‐equilibrium, Mg‐containing lightweight HEAs drives phase segregation, leading to the formation of dispersed Mg‐rich intermetallic compounds that mediate changes in corrosion and high-temperature oxidation behavior by establishing a sacrificial, protective oxide layer.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast, metastable single-phase solid solution HEA with homogeneous elemental distribution and density below 6 g/cm³.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled thermal aging (annealing) treatment at elevated temperatures relevant to oxidation exposure.
generation.conditions: Samples produced via non-equilibrium processing (e.g., rapid solidification or induction melting) under identical conditions, then exposed to controlled high-temperature and corrosive environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic phases, particularly along grain boundaries and within the matrix.
generation.mechanism: Elevated temperature provides the driving force for the metastable solid solution to decompose. The resulting Mg-rich intermetallic compounds oxidize preferentially, forming a continuous or semi-continuous sacrificial oxide scale that alters the alloy’s corrosion dynamics and enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-cast baseline, thermally aged samples will exhibit a refined microstructure with detectable Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates, a more stable and adherent oxide layer during high-temperature oxidation, and altered corrosion rates due to local changes in electrochemical behavior from the evolved phases.
generation.baseline: As-cast Mg-containing lightweight HEA with homogeneous microstructure lacking pronounced Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to HEAs designed for densities below 6 g/cm³ and tested under comparable aggressive oxidation and corrosive conditions; results may not extend to alloys with significantly differing compositions or processing histories.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of the corrosion and oxidation improvements is uncertain due to possible interactions with minor alloying elements and nanoscale phase distribution effects that require detailed characterization.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of Mg-containing HEA samples via rapid solidification. Subject one set to a defined thermal aging treatment and keep the other as-cast. Characterize both sets using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) to document microstructural changes, and perform high-temperature oxidation tests (e.g., mass gain and oxide adhesion tests) as well as electrochemical corrosion assessments.
measurements: Phase and grain boundary analysis via TEM/SEM-EDS
Composition and morphology of oxide scales via XRD and SEM
Corrosion current density via potentiodynamic polarization
Mass gain rate during high-temperature oxidation tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermally aged samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in Mg-rich intermetallic formation and no corresponding improvement (or predictable change) in high-temperature oxidation stability and corrosion behavior compared to the as-cast baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.

chosen.approach: Elemental alloy design and composition variation in Mg‐containing lightweight HEAs
